note: Configuration case, carrier-Ethernet VPN, MEF service side. One multipoint (E-LAN) Ethernet service over three UNIs, described in the MEF service view. Carries two false-cognate traps (network-segment vs ethernet-segment; MAC-learning vs MAC-mobility) and one opaque vendor attribute. ref=null marks an opaque item or native gap.

concepts.label: ethernet-service
concepts.gloss: the multipoint Ethernet service connecting the customer's UNIs
concepts.example: the ACME E-LAN across three sites

concepts.label: UNI
concepts.gloss: the physical demarcation where a customer site attaches to the carrier network
concepts.example: UNI at the ACME headquarters, 1 GbE

concepts.label: EVC-endpoint
concepts.gloss: the endpoint of the Ethernet service at one UNI
concepts.example: the ACME E-LAN endpoint at UNI-HQ

concepts.label: network-segment
concepts.gloss: the customer VLAN broadcast segment carried by the service
concepts.example: customer VLAN 200, one broadcast domain across the E-LAN

concepts.label: bandwidth-profile
concepts.gloss: the ingress rate profile (CIR/EIR) policed at a UNI
concepts.example: CIR 200 Mbit/s, EIR 50 Mbit/s at UNI-HQ

concepts.label: class-of-service
concepts.gloss: the class-of-service forwarding treatment for frames on the service
concepts.example: the real-time CoS mapped from customer PCP 5

concepts.label: MAC-learning
concepts.gloss: how the service learns customer source-MAC addresses at a UNI to build its forwarding

concepts.label: service-mtu
concepts.gloss: the maximum service frame size carried end to end
concepts.example: 9100-byte jumbo frames on the ACME E-LAN

concepts.label: service-availability
concepts.gloss: the availability objective for the service (service-view self-extension; no network-model counterpart)
